doc.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023

chapter: James Taylor band and big band
title: Writing horn parts for James Taylor
summary: Marini and Walt Fowler organically build horn parts for Taylor's songs; Marini plays bass flute, flute and clarinet, including a clarinet solo on 'It's Just Like Falling Off a Log'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Who writes the horn parts for these?

Walt and I do. And you know that’s been another thing because it’s so naturally organic. I’ll play something and Walt will go — because James will — at first there were no horn parts. So now we’re up to in the 90s. And James will, at this point he’ll say you know I think this tune is horn-worthy, and the rhythm section will start rehearsing it and Walt and I will — I’ll play something, Walt will play something, we’re like, “Let’s remember that.” And then we go into a hotel room or a room in the venue and sit down and listen to the track and start playing and sketching out stuff and the next thing you know we have a horn part. And without — totally without friction. That’s been the one delight with James, it’s so organic and natural. It just feels great you know.
You must be cognizant of course of when he is singing and regarding the horn parts.

Oh yeah. Yeah. But you know like at this point, between us, just between Walt and I, Jesus, we’ve played for everybody you know. And so we’ve had the opportunity to hear and play what good horn parts are about. So we already have a clear idea of where we should play and where we shouldn’t. And you know James, and it’s not always that you shouldn’t play when the singer is singing, ‘cause sometimes you do play when the singer is singing. It’s not just filling in the holes, it’s complementing and adding something. And James is very cool, he’ll say, “I don’t think that — maybe we should do something else there” and he’ll have suggestions and they’re always great. So yeah it’s been — I play, I have juicy parts on bass flute, alto flute, flute, clarinet, and then the four saxophones. So it’s not often that you know you have a bass flute in a pop band that’s meaningful and fun to play. Yeah, the last tour we did this tune from the standards album, “It’s Like Falling Off a Log,” you know “It’s Just Like Falling Off a Log,” you know it’s a tune that James knew from the 30’s cartoon. And I played a clarinet solo on the record and so I was playing that clarinet solo and then I suggested that maybe Walt should play like a straight mute solo, to play it with me, and it’s this charming thing. And we got applause for it every night. And 52 concerts I never screwed it up, so that made me feel good. Because the clarinet is perilous.
